mainTopic: The source and limits of טומאת התהום for the תמיד, the נזיר and the פסח, and where an impure פסח is burned
overview: The amud opens by rejecting a קל וחומר that would allow טומאת התהום for a כהן bringing communal offerings, because a קל וחומר cannot be built on a הלכה למשה מסיני. רבא instead learns the leniency for the תמיד from a גזירה שוה of "מועדו" from the פסח. The גמרא then looks for a verse that teaches טומאת התהום itself: רבי אלעזר points to "עליו" by the נזיר, and רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש point to "לכם" and "דרך" by the פסח. A ברייתא says that if even one person anywhere knew of the corpse, it is not טומאת התהום, and none of the three readings fits that test. So the גמרא concludes that טומאת התהום is a received הלכה and the verses are only an אסמכתא. מר בר רב אשי's ruling on whether the ציץ helps when the impurity was known before the זריקה is corrected to say that it does help, and the גמרא then studies the ברייתא about a corpse found across a road, with its many limits. A new משנה explains where an impure or leftover פסח is burned, and רבי יוסי בר חנינא says the public burning is meant to embarrass careless owners. The amud ends as the גמרא begins a contradiction from meat carried out of ירושלים, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the proposed reasoning: the כהן should certainly be allowed טומאת התהום
steps.stepSummary: The closing words of a קל וחומר. A כהן offering communal sacrifices is already allowed to work even with known טומאה, so he should certainly be allowed hidden טומאת התהום.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it only logical that טומאת התהום is permitted for him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a proof it started on the previous amud. The proof argues that the כהן should be allowed טומאת התהום fully, even when pure כהנים are available.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full argument runs like this. For a נזיר and for someone bringing a פסח, known טומאה is never allowed, yet טומאת התהום is allowed. For communal offerings, known טומאה is sometimes allowed (טומאה הותרה בציבור), so hidden טומאת התהום should surely be allowed there too. That is the structure of a קל וחומר: if the stricter case is lenient, the more lenient case is certainly lenient.

keyTerms.meaning: "Isn't it logical?" This is the standard closing phrase of a קַל וָחוֹמֶר.
"Impurity of the deep": impurity from a hidden corpse that nobody knew about.
Was permitted.

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of the argument. The first half of this קל וחומר (about the נזיר and the פסח) appeared on the previous amud, so the words "אינו דין" are its punchline, not a new idea.

phrases.english: Is it not logical
phrases.notes: This is the usual way a קל וחומר wraps up its argument.

phrases.english: that impurity of the deep is permitted for him!
phrases.notes: "Him" is the כהן offering communal sacrifices such as the תמיד.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁהוּתְּרָה לוֹ טוּמְאַת הַתְּהוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a קל וחומר begun in the text on the previous amud.
steps.raayaObject: That טומאת התהום is permitted for a כהן offering communal sacrifices, even when pure כהנים are available.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from the cases of נזיר and עושה פסח, based on the fact that known טומאה is permitted in communal settings.

steps.title: Rejection: you cannot build a logical argument on a tradition from Sinai
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. טומאת התהום is a הלכה למשה מסיני, and a קל וחומר cannot be derived from a הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: Do we really derive a קל וחומר from a הלכה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the proof from Step 1 by questioning the method it used, not its conclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The leniency of טומאת התהום for נזיר and פסח is known only from an oral tradition given to משה at סיני, not from logic or a verse. A rule like that cannot serve as the starting point for logical extension. So the entire קל וחומר falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: "And do we really derive?" This is a challenging question.
Logical inference from a stricter case to a more lenient one, or the reverse.
Here it means הֲלָכָה לְמֹשֶׁה מִסִּינַי, an oral law given at סיני.

steps.confusionAlert: Even though this is phrased as a question, it is really a rejection. The גמרא means: "We do NOT derive a קל וחומר from a הלכה."

phrases.english: They say: And do we derive
phrases.notes: This question is really a way of saying no, we can't learn it like that.

phrases.english: an a fortiori inference from a halakha (from Sinai)?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: וּמִי דָּיְינִינַן קַל וָחוֹמֶר מֵהֲלָכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר of Step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The entire קל וחומר proof. The conclusion itself is not rejected, only this way of reaching it.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The base case (טומאת התהום for נזיר and פסח) is a הלכה למשה מסיני, and a קל וחומר may not be built on a הלכה.

steps.title: Proof from a ברייתא: רבי אליעזר tells רבי עקיבא the same rule
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי אליעזר rejected a קל וחומר from רבי עקיבא for exactly this reason. The rule that a bone the size of a barley grain makes a person impure is a הלכה, so a רביעית of blood cannot be learned from it by קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי אליעזר said to him, "עקיבא, the bone the size of a barley grain is a הלכה, and you learn a רביעית of blood from it by קל וחומר? One may not derive a קל וחומר from a הלכה!"
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an earlier source to back up its rejection in Step 2. It shows that the principle "no קל וחומר from a הלכה" is already established.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא had argued that if a tiny bone obligates a נזיר to shave, a רביעית of blood should certainly do the same. רבי אליעזר answered that the bone rule is a הלכה למשה מסיני, so it cannot be the basis of a קל וחומר. This is the same objection the גמרא raised against the proof in Step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: A bone the size of a barley grain. It makes a נָזִיר impure because of a הֲלָכָה.
A quarter-לוֹג of blood from a corpse.
"We do not derive."

phrases.english: Wasn't it taught: Rabbi Eliezer said to him:
Akiva, a bone the size of a barley grain is a halakha (from Sinai),
and a quarter-log of blood you derive by a fortiori?
phrases.notes: Said with surprise: you want to derive the blood rule from the bone rule?

phrases.english: But one may not derive an a fortiori inference from a halakha!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides a source for the rejection in Step 2.
steps.raayaObject: The principle that אין דנין קל וחומר מהלכה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording רבי אליעזר's reply to רבי עקיבא about a נזיר and a רביעית of blood.
steps.whyThisMatters: "אין דנין קל וחומר מהלכה" is a general rule of Torah interpretation that appears across ש"ס.

steps.title: רבא's new source: a גזירה שוה from the word "מועדו"
steps.stepSummary: Since the קל וחומר failed, רבא learns the rule a different way. The word "מועדו" (its appointed time) appears both by the פסח and by the תמיד, so the תמיד shares the פסח's leniency of טומאת התהום.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: We learn it from the word "מועדו", "מועדו", from the פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא replaces the rejected proof with a new one. The same conclusion now comes from a linked word in the verses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה is not built on logic. It is a link between two verses that share a word. Because both the פסח and the תמיד are commanded "במועדו", the rule allowing טומאת התהום by the פסח carries over to the תמיד. This avoids the problem of building a קל וחומר on a הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: "Rather." It signals that the previous approach is dropped.
He learns or derives.
"Its appointed time." This word appears by the פֶּסַח (במדבר ט) and by the תָּמִיד (במדבר כח).
A derivation from the same word appearing in two places.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
It is derived from "its appointed time" / "its appointed time," from the Paschal lamb.
phrases.notes: The same words show up by the פסח and by the תמיד, so we learn one from the other. That's called a גזירה שוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a replacement source after the קל וחומר was rejected in Steps 2 and 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replacing the source: the method changes from a קל וחומר to a גזירה שוה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The leniency for the כהן was learned by a קל וחומר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The leniency for the תמיד is learned by a גזירה שוה of "מועדו" "מועדו" from the פסח, not by a קל וחומר.
steps.whatToRemember: Communal offerings like the תמיד are allowed with טומאת התהום. The source is not a קל וחומר but the גזירה שוה of "מועדו" "מועדו" from the פסח.

steps.title: Where is טומאת התהום itself hinted in the Torah?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where in the verses the basic rule of טומאת התהום (for the נזיר and the פסח) can be found.
steps.simpleTranslation: And טומאת התהום itself, where is it written?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a new question about the root rule itself. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the גמרא discussed extending טומאת התהום to the תמיד. Now it goes back to the base rule and asks for a hint in the Torah's text.

keyTerms.meaning: "Itself." The focus returns to the main subject.
"Where is it written?"

phrases.english: And impurity of the deep itself,
where is it written?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the extension of the rule (to the תמיד) to the base rule itself.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The verse that hints at the leniency of טומאת התהום.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: "עליו" means the death must be clearly known to him
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר points to the verse about the נזיר, "וכי ימות מת עליו". The word "עליו" teaches that the rule applies only when the death is clear and known to the person, not when the corpse is hidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: The verse says, "And if a person dies beside him" (עליו), meaning when it is clear to him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the question from Step 5 with a verse in פרשת נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "עליו" (beside him, or upon him) is read as "מחוורת עליו", meaning clear and known to him. So the נזיר's obligations of טומאה apply only to a known corpse. A hidden corpse, which is טומאת התהום, does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: "Beside him" or "upon him."
Clear, known for certain.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said: The verse states:
"And if a person dies beside him"
phrases.notes: במדבר ו:ט, in the section about the נזיר.

phrases.english: meaning, when it is clear to him.
phrases.notes: A corpse that is not clearly known to him is excluded.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word "עליו" in "וכי ימות מת עליו" limits the נזיר's טומאה to a death that is clearly known (מחוורת עליו), which excludes טומאת התהום.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אלעזר, the Torah's hint for טומאת התהום is the word "עליו" in פרשת נזיר: only a clearly known corpse counts.

steps.title: We have a source for the נזיר. What about the פסח?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes it found a source for טומאת התהום by the נזיר, and asks for a source for one who brings the פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: We found a source for the נזיר. For someone bringing the פסח, where do we learn it from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up what it already found (a source for the נזיר) and asks for the second half: a source for the פסח. This sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6, רבי אלעזר used the word עליו, but that verse is only about a נזיר. The פסח is a separate topic in the Torah, so it needs its own source in its own verses.

keyTerms.meaning: We have found (a source for one case)
One who brings (offers) the קרבן פסח
From where do we know it?

phrases.english: We have found [a source for] a nazir.
phrases.notes: Refers to the source from עליו in step 6.

phrases.english: One who brings the Pesach, from where do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 6's source for the נזיר and asks for the parallel source for the פסח.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A verse showing that טומאת התהום does not disqualify one bringing the פסח.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the word לכם means clear to you
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן learns it from the word לכם in the verse about פסח שני: the impurity must be clear to you.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: The verse says 'or on a far road, of you (לכם)'. This means the impurity must be clear to you.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question with a verse from the section on פסח שני. He reads the word לכם as 'clear to you'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse lists who must push off his פסח, and the word לכם is extra. רבי יוחנן reads it as: only impurity that is known to you stops you from bringing the פסח. Hidden impurity (טומאת התהום) does not.

keyTerms.meaning: On a far road, of you (במדבר ט:י)
When it is clear (known) to you

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said,
the verse says: "on a far road, of you (lachem)"
phrases.notes: במדבר ט:י, about who brings פסח שני.

phrases.english: meaning: when it is clear to you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word לכם teaches that only impurity clear to you holds back the פסח.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: impurity is like a road, out in the open
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש learns it from the word דרך: just as a road is open, the impurity must be out in the open.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: 'Like a road.' Just as a road is out in the open, so too the impurity must be out in the open.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives a different source for the same rule. He reads the word דרך (road), which sits next to 'impure' in the verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A road is open and visible to everyone. Since the verse puts 'impure' next to 'road', ריש לקיש says the impurity must also be open and visible. Hidden impurity is not included. He and רבי יוחנן agree that hidden impurity is excluded for the פסח, but they learn it from different words, and the next steps show that each reading sets a different test for what counts as known.

keyTerms.meaning: Like a road
In the open, visible

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
Like a road.
phrases.notes: He reads the word 'road' as describing the kind of impurity.

phrases.english: Just as a road is in the open,
so too impurity must also be in the open.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אָמַר: כְּדֶרֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 7's question, using a different word than רבי יוחנן.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word דרך teaches that only open, visible impurity holds back the פסח.

steps.title: A ברייתא defines hidden impurity: nobody in the world knows of it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: טומאת התהום is only impurity that nobody in the whole world knows about. If even one person anywhere knows, it is not טומאת התהום.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: What is טומאת התהום? Any impurity that no one at the end of the world knows about. If one person at the end of the world knows about it, it is not טומאת התהום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא to challenge the sources it just gave. This line only sets up the challenge; the next steps show the clash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא sets a strict test: one person anywhere who knows is enough to make it 'known'. The sources above were about what is clear to 'him' or to 'you'. The question now is whether those readings fit this test.

keyTerms.meaning: Hidden impurity, like a corpse buried with nobody aware of it
Knew about it, was aware of it
At the end of the world (even very far away)

steps.confusionAlert: 'One person at the end of the world' does not mean the person must be far away. It means that even if only one person anywhere at all knows about the corpse, it is already not hidden.

phrases.english: They challenged:
What is impurity of the deep?
Any [impurity] that was not known
by even one person at the end of the world.
If one person at the end of the world knew of it,
this is not impurity of the deep.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to test the sources of steps 6, 8, and 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The sources from עליו, לכם, and דרך
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says one person anywhere knowing makes it not hidden. The verse readings seem to set a different number of people who must know.

steps.title: The clash with רבי אלעזר: he needs the person himself to know
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי אלעזר, who read עליו as 'clear to him', it should stay טומאת התהום until the person himself knows. Another person knowing should not matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי אלעזר, who said 'clear to him', it should stay hidden until he himself knows.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how the ברייתא clashes with רבי אלעזר from step 6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עליו means 'to him', so by רבי אלעזר only the person's own knowledge should count. But the ברייתא says any one person in the world knowing is enough. So the ברייתא seems to go against רבי אלעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: When it is clear to him
Until he himself knows

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Elazar, who said:
"when it is clear to him"
[it should stay hidden] until he himself knows.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ברייתא of step 10 against רבי אלעזר's reading.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: עליו points to the person's own knowledge, but the ברייתא counts any one person's knowledge.

steps.title: The clash with רבי יוחנן: the plural לכם means two people
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי יוחנן, who read לכם as 'clear to you' (plural), it should stay טומאת התהום until two people know. The ברייתא says one is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי יוחנן, who said 'לכם, clear to you', it should stay hidden until two people know about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the same kind of clash with רבי יוחנן from step 8. The challenge continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לכם is plural ('to you all'), which suggests at least two people must know. But the ברייתא says one person knowing is enough. So the ברייתא seems to go against רבי יוחנן too.

keyTerms.meaning: Until two people know about it

steps.confusionAlert: The point here is grammar: לכם is plural. That is why רבי יוחנן's reading seems to need two people, while עליו (singular) seemed to need the person himself.

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Yochanan, who said:
"lachem", when it is clear to you (plural)
[it should stay hidden] until two people know of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, דְּאָמַר: לָכֶם, בִּמְחֻוֶּורֶת לָכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ברייתא of step 10 against רבי יוחנן's reading, parallel to step 11.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The plural לכם suggests two people must know, but the ברייתא says one person anywhere is enough.

steps.title: The challenge also hits ריש לקיש's 'road' reading
steps.stepSummary: According to ריש לקיש, who learned from דרך, the impurity should stay טומאת התהום until the whole world knows about it. That clashes with the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to ריש לקיש, who said 'like a road,' it should stay hidden impurity until everyone in the world knows.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא aims the same ברייתא at the third source. It shows that ריש לקיש's reading does not fit either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש said the impurity must be like a road, open to everyone. If so, it should stop being טומאת התהום only once everyone knows about it. But the ברייתא says one person knowing is already enough, so this reading would stretch טומאת התהום much further than the ברייתא allows.

keyTerms.meaning: Like a road, meaning out in the open for everyone
The whole world, everyone
Until they know

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish,
who said: 'like a road'
phrases.notes: His source from step 9: the impurity must be open like a road.

phrases.english: it should be hidden impurity until the whole world knows.
phrases.notes: But the ברייתא says one person knowing is enough.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ, דְּאָמַר: כְּדֶרֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third and final application of the ברייתא challenge, after steps 11 and 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's derivation from the word דרך
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Like a road' implies public knowledge by everyone is needed. The ברייתא says even one person's knowledge removes the status of טומאת התהום.

steps.title: Hidden impurity is a received tradition, and the verses are only a hint
steps.stepSummary: Since none of the verse readings fits the ברייתא, the גמרא concludes that טומאת התהום is a הלכה learned by tradition. The verses only serve as an אסמכתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, they learned the rule of hidden impurity as a received law, and the verse is just a support.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on finding the true source in a verse. It says the rule is an oral tradition (a הלכה למשה מסיני), and the verses are only a hint.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three readings (עליו, לכם, דרך) gave the wrong number of people who must know. Since the rule's details do not come from the verse, the rule must come from tradition. Then the exact details (one person knowing is enough) come from that tradition, not from the wording of a verse.

keyTerms.meaning: They learned it as a received law (tradition)
Merely a support or hint, not the real source
The verse
Rather (introduces a new approach after rejecting the old one)

steps.whatToRemember: טומאת התהום is a הלכה from tradition. The verses about עליו, לכם, and דרך are only an אסמכתא. That is why one person knowing is enough to remove the hidden status.
steps.confusionAlert: An אסמכתא does not mean the verse is meaningless. It means the verse is a hint the חכמים attached to the law, but the law itself does not depend on reading the verse exactly.

phrases.english: Rather, hidden impurity
they learned it as a received law,
phrases.notes: A tradition from Sinai, not derived from a verse.

phrases.english: and the verse is merely a support.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, טוּמְאַת הַתְּהוֹם הִלְכְתָא גְּמִירִי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the three challenges by moving the source from the verses to tradition.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The source of טומאת התהום is an oral הלכה. The verses are only hints, so the ברייתא's 'one person' rule stands without conflict.

steps.title: The ציץ helps only if the impurity was discovered after the sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי rules that the ציץ helps for hidden impurity only when the impurity became known after the זריקה. If it was known before, the ציץ does not help.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בר רב אשי said: They only taught this when he found out after the sprinkling. Once the blood was sprinkled, it was sprinkled properly. But if he found out before the sprinkling, it does not bring acceptance.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא adds a limit to the rule that the ציץ helps a נזיר and someone bringing a קרבן פסח who had hidden impurity. It works only if they found out after the blood was sprinkled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reasoning is that at the moment of the זריקה nobody knew about the impurity, so the sprinkling was done correctly. After the fact, the ציץ covers it. If the impurity was already known before the זריקה, then sprinkling would be done knowingly on an impure person's behalf, and the ציץ does not fix that.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this when (a limiting formula)
Sprinkling of the קרבן's blood on the מזבח
It was sprinkled properly
Brings acceptance (here, the ציץ making the קרבן accepted)

steps.whyThisMatters: This changes the ציץ's help from a full permission into an after-the-fact fix. The next step tests whether that limit is correct.

phrases.english: Mar bar Rav Ashi said:
They only taught this
when it became known to him after the sprinkling,
because when the blood was sprinkled,
it was sprinkled properly,
phrases.notes: At that moment nobody knew about the impurity.

phrases.english: but if it became known to him before the sprinkling,
the ציץ does not bring acceptance.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion about when the ציץ's help for טומאת התהום applies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ציץ helps a נזיר or someone bringing a קרבן פסח with hidden impurity only if the impurity was discovered after the זריקה.

steps.title: A ברייתא calls him pure even before the sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that someone who finds a corpse across a road is טמא for תרומה but טהור for a נזיר and a קרבן פסח. It adds that 'טמא' and 'טהור' are rulings for the future. That suggests the ציץ helps even before the זריקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him: If someone finds a corpse lying across the width of a road, for תרומה he is impure. For a נזיר and someone bringing the פסח, he is pure. And every 'impure' and 'pure' is for the future.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא to challenge מר בר רב אשי. The ברייתא seems to allow the person to go ahead even before the blood is sprinkled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The corpse lies across the whole road, so the passerby surely became impure, but the impurity was hidden. The ברייתא calls him טהור for נזיר and פסח, and says such rulings apply 'for the future,' meaning לכתחילה. Here he already knows about the corpse before any זריקה, yet he is called טהור, which contradicts מר בר רב אשי.

keyTerms.meaning: Across the width of the road (so he could not avoid it)
The כהן's portion, which an impure person may not eat
A person who took a vow of נזירות
For the future, meaning a ruling one may act on from the start

steps.confusionAlert: 'טהור' here does not mean he is pure for everything. He is still טמא for תרומה. He is treated as pure only for a נזיר and a קרבן פסח, where the ציץ covers hidden impurity.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
One who finds a corpse lying
across the width of the road,
phrases.notes: So anyone who walked there surely passed over it.

phrases.english: for תרומה, he is impure.
For a נזיר and one bringing the פסח, he is pure.
And every 'impure' and 'pure'
is for the future.
phrases.notes: So it applies from the start (לכתחילה), even before the זריקה, and that's a problem for מר בר רב אשי.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: הַמּוֹצֵא מֵת מוּשְׁכָּב לְרׇחְבּוֹ שֶׁל דֶּרֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the limit that מר בר רב אשי set in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: מר בר רב אשי's rule that the ציץ helps only if the impurity is discovered after the זריקה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא calls the person טהור for נזיר and פסח 'for the future' (לכתחילה), even though he already knows about the corpse before any זריקה. That implies the ציץ helps even when the impurity is known before the sprinkling.

steps.title: מר בר רב אשי's statement is rewritten: the ציץ helps even before the זריקה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the first version of מר בר רב אשי's ruling and gives a corrected version. In this version, the ציץ helps even if the impurity became known before the זריקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if this was said, it was said like this: מר בר רב אשי said: Do not think the ציץ helps only when the person found out after the זריקה, and not when he found out before. Rather, even if he found out before the זריקה, it still helps.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from the last step proved the first version of מר בר רב אשי wrong. So the גמרא says his statement must have been the opposite, and restates it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the old version, the ציץ helped only if the impurity was discovered after the זריקה. The ברייתא calls the person טהור for פסח as a ruling for the future, which means he may bring the קרבן even though he already knows. So the corrected version says that knowing before the זריקה does not block the ציץ for טומאת התהום.

keyTerms.meaning: If it was said, it was said like this (a formula that rewrites an earlier statement)
The gold plate worn by the כהן גדול, which brings forgiveness for certain kinds of impurity
Throwing the blood of the קרבן on the מזבח
Brings acceptance or forgiveness, so the קרבן counts

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions. The first version (step 15) was rejected. The final version is that the ציץ helps for טומאת התהום even if the impurity was known before the זריקה.
steps.whatToRemember: Final ruling of מר בר רב אשי: for טומאת התהום, the ציץ helps even if the impurity became known before the זריקה.

phrases.english: Rather, if it was stated, it was stated like this:
Mar bar Rav Ashi said:

phrases.aramaic: לָא תֵּימָא נוֹדַע לוֹ לְאַחַר זְרִיקָה
phrases.english: Do not say that when it became known to him after the sprinkling
that is when it (the frontplate) brings acceptance,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל נוֹדַע לוֹ לִפְנֵי זְרִיקָה — לֹא מְרַצֶּה,
phrases.english: but if it became known to him before the sprinkling, it does not bring acceptance,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ נוֹדַע לוֹ לִפְנֵי זְרִיקָה — מְרַצֶּה.
phrases.english: rather, even if it became known to him before the sprinkling, it brings acceptance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 16 by replacing the version of מר בר רב אשי given in step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rewriting the statement (אי איתמר הכי איתמר)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ציץ helps only if the impurity became known after the זריקה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ציץ helps for טומאת התהום even if the impurity became known before the זריקה.

steps.title: Back to the ברייתא: a corpse lying across the road
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the ברייתא it just quoted in order to study it on its own terms. The person is טמא for תרומה but טהור for a נזיר and for someone bringing a קרבן פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now the matter itself: If someone finds a dead body lying across the width of a road, he is טמא for תרומה, but טהור for a נזיר and for someone bringing a קרבן פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The word גופא tells us the גמרא is going back to the ברייתא to explain its details. This step restates the basic case and sets up the limits that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The body blocks the whole road, so the walker almost surely passed over it. That is why he is טמא for תרומה. For a נזיר and for פסח, the special leniency of טומאת התהום applies, because nobody knew about this body, so he is treated as טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself: going back to study a source that was just quoted
Lying across the full width of the road
The holy portion given to a כהן, which must be eaten in purity
A person who took a vow not to drink wine and not to become impure from a corpse

phrases.english: The matter itself:

phrases.aramaic: הַמּוֹצֵא מֵת מוּשְׁכָּב לְרׇחְבּוֹ שֶׁל דֶּרֶךְ,
phrases.english: One who finds a corpse lying across the width of the road,
with regard to teruma, he is impure;
with regard to a nazirite and one who brings the Paschal lamb, he is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא quoted in step 16 to study it on its own.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A corpse across the road makes the walker טמא for תרומה, but he is טהור for נזיר and פסח.

steps.title: First limit: only when there was no way to get around the body
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא limits its ruling of טמא for תרומה to a case where the walker had no room to pass. If there was room, he is טהור even for תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When is this true? When he had no room to pass without going over the body. But if there was room to pass, he is טהור even for תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds its first limit to the ruling that he is טמא for תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he could have walked around the body, then it is only a doubt whether he passed over it. A doubt about impurity in a public place is treated as טהור. So even for תרומה he stays טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case are these words said? (introduces a limit on a ruling)
Room to pass by
A doubt about impurity in a public place, which is treated as טהור

phrases.english: In what case is this said?
Where he has no room to pass by.
But if there is room to pass by,
even with regard to teruma he is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים — שֶׁאֵין לוֹ מָקוֹם לַעֲבוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the ruling of step 18 that he is טמא for תרומה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If there was room to walk around the body, he is טהור even for תרומה.

steps.title: Second limit: only when the body was whole
steps.stepSummary: The walker is טמא only if the body was found whole. If it was broken into pieces, he is טהור, because maybe he walked between the pieces.
steps.simpleTranslation: When is this true? When he found the body whole. But if it was broken or taken apart, he is טהור, because maybe he walked between the parts.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a second limit to the ruling that he is טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A whole body blocking the road means he surely passed over it. If the body is in pieces, there may be gaps, so it is possible he never went over any part. That makes it a doubt, so he is טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: Whole, in one piece
Broken and taken apart into separate pieces
Between the parts

phrases.english: In what case is this said?
Where he found it whole.
But if it was broken or taken apart, he is pure,
for perhaps he passed between the parts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second limit after the limit of step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A broken or dismembered body leaves room for doubt, so the walker is טהור.

steps.title: A grave is different: it joins the pieces together
steps.stepSummary: If the broken body is inside a grave, the walker is still טמא, because the grave joins all the pieces into one unit.
steps.simpleTranslation: But in a grave, even if the body is broken or taken apart, he is טמא, because the grave joins it together.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives an exception to the leniency for a broken body: the leniency does not apply inside a grave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Out in the open, the gaps between the pieces create a doubt. A grave counts as one unit with the body, so passing over any part of the grave counts as passing over the body. The gaps no longer help, and he is טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: A grave
Joins it together into one unit

steps.whatToRemember: The walker is טמא for תרומה only when he could not avoid the body and the body was whole. A grave is the exception: it joins even a broken body into one unit.

phrases.english: But in a grave, even if broken or taken apart, he is impure,
because the grave joins it together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Makes an exception to the leniency for a broken body given in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Inside a grave, even a broken body makes the walker טמא, because the grave joins the pieces.

steps.title: The broken-body leniency applies only to someone walking on foot
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא limits the ruling that a walker past a broken body is טהור. It applies only to someone walking on his feet. A person carrying a load or riding an animal is טמא, because he surely touched or overshadowed the body.
steps.simpleTranslation: When is this said? When the person was walking on his feet. But if he was carrying a load or riding, he is טמא. A person on foot might not touch the body and might not pass over it. But a person carrying a load or riding cannot avoid touching it or passing over it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds one more limit to the leniency from Step 20. It says the broken-body leniency covers only a person walking on foot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 20, the walker was טהור because maybe he stepped between the pieces. That doubt only works for someone walking carefully on foot. A loaded person sways and a rider sits high and wide, so it is certain he touched the body or passed over it (אהל), and he is טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case are these words said? (a formula that limits a ruling)
Walking on his feet
Carrying a load
Riding an animal
Will overshadow, meaning pass over the body and become טמא through אֹהֶל

phrases.english: In what case are these words said?
phrases.notes: This narrows the ruling that the walker is טהור if the body was broken into pieces.

phrases.english: Regarding one who walks on his feet,
but one who is carrying a load or riding is impure,
because one who walks on his feet,
it is possible that he will not touch and will not overshadow,
but one who is carrying a load or riding,

phrases.aramaic: אִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁלֹּא יִגַּע וְלֹא יַאֲהִיל.
phrases.english: it is impossible that he will not touch and will not overshadow.
phrases.notes: A loaded person does not walk straight, and a rider takes up more space.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another limit to the broken-body leniency of Step 20, after Step 21's grave exception.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The broken-body leniency applies only to someone on foot. A person carrying a load or riding is טמא, because he certainly touched the body or overshadowed it.

steps.title: The leniency for a נזיר and a פסח applies only to an unknown impurity
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא limits the ruling that a נזיר and someone bringing a קרבן פסח stay טהור. This applies only to טומאת התהום. If the טומאה was known, he is טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: When is this said? With טומאת התהום, a completely hidden impurity. But with a known impurity, he is טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now limits its other leniency from Step 18, that the walker counts as טהור for a נזיר and a קרבן פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a special leniency (a הלכה) for a נזיר and a פסח when the טומאה was totally hidden, called טומאת התהום. If the dead body was known to someone, the leniency does not apply, even if this particular walker did not know about it.

keyTerms.meaning: Impurity of the deep, a dead body hidden so well that nobody knew about it
A known impurity, a body someone was aware of

steps.confusionAlert: 'Known' does not mean known to the walker himself. It means known to anyone at all, as the next step explains.

phrases.english: In what case are these words said?
phrases.notes: Now it narrows the ruling that a נזיר and a קרבן פסח stay טהור.

phrases.english: Regarding impurity of the deep,
but with a known impurity, he is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the תרומה-related limits back to Step 18's ruling about a נזיר and a פסח, and limits it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The leniency for a נזיר and a קרבן פסח applies only to טומאת התהום. With a known impurity, he is טמא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the whole sugya cares about whether the body was hidden. The special leniency for a פסח and a נזיר depends on it.

steps.title: Defining טומאת התהום: nobody anywhere knew about it
steps.stepSummary: טומאת התהום means a body that no one in the world knew about. If even one person at the far end of the world knew about it, it is not טומאת התהום.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is טומאת התהום? Any body that not even one person at the end of the world knew about. But if one person at the end of the world knew about it, it is not טומאת התהום.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא defines the term it just used, טומאת התהום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is extremely strict. If even one person anywhere ever knew about the body, it counts as a known טומאה and the leniency is lost.

keyTerms.meaning: Was aware of it, knew about it
At the end of the world, meaning anywhere at all

phrases.english: And which is impurity of the deep?
Any case in which not
even one person at the end of the world knew about it.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הִכִּיר בָּהּ אֶחָד בְּסוֹף הָעוֹלָם —
phrases.english: But if one person at the end of the world knew about it,
this is not impurity of the deep.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the term טומאת התהום used in Step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: טומאת התהום is a body that no person anywhere knew about. If anyone at all knew, it is not טומאת התהום.

steps.title: Which hiding places count as טומאת התהום
steps.stepSummary: A body found buried in straw, dirt, or pebbles counts as טומאת התהום. A body found in water, in a dark place, or in cracks of rocks does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he found the body buried in straw, in dirt, or in pebbles, this is טומאת התהום. If it was in water, in a dark place, or in the cracks of rocks, it is not טומאת התהום.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives practical examples showing how to decide whether a body was truly unknown.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A body covered by straw, dirt, or pebbles could have been buried suddenly, for example by a landslide, so likely no one ever saw it. Water, dark places, and rock cracks are hard to reach, but over time someone probably passed by and saw the body, so we cannot assume it was unknown.

keyTerms.meaning: Buried, hidden
Straw, hay
Pebbles
Cracks in the rocks

phrases.english: If he found it buried in straw,
in dirt, or in pebbles,
this is impurity of the deep.
phrases.notes: It could have been covered suddenly, so likely no one ever saw it.

phrases.english: In water, in darkness, in the cracks of the rocks,
this is not impurity of the deep.
phrases.notes: Over time someone may have seen it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the definition from Step 24 to real hiding places.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A body buried in straw, dirt, or pebbles is טומאת התהום. A body in water, darkness, or rock cracks is not.

steps.title: The rule of טומאת התהום applies only to a dead body
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by saying the leniency of טומאת התהום was said only about a מת, not about other kinds of טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said the rule of טומאת התהום only for a dead body.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא closes by limiting the whole concept of טומאת התהום to a dead body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Other sources of טומאה, like a שרץ, do not get this leniency even if they were completely hidden. The special leniency is only for טומאת מת.

keyTerms.meaning: A dead human body
Only

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא gives several limits: the broken-body leniency is only for someone on foot, the נזיר/פסח leniency is only for טומאת התהום, טומאת התהום means no one anywhere knew about the body, and the rule applies only to a מת.

phrases.english: And they did not say impurity of the deep
except for a dead body alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא אָמְרוּ טוּמְאַת הַתְּהוֹם אֶלָּא לְמֵת בִּלְבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the ברייתא's discussion of טומאת התהום by limiting it to a מת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The leniency of טומאת התהום applies only to a dead body, not to other sources of טומאה.

steps.title: A fully or mostly impure פסח is burned in front of the בירה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if the whole קרבן פסח, or most of it, became טמא, it is burned in front of the בירה using wood from the מזבח's woodpile.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If the whole פסח or most of it became טמא, we burn it in front of the בירה, using wood from the מערכה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It tells us where and how to burn a קרבן פסח when all of it, or most of it, became טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קרבן that became טמא cannot be eaten and must be burned. When all or most of the פסח is טמא, the burning is done in a public place, in front of the בירה (the בית המקדש area). The wood comes from the מערכה, the wood set aside for the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Became ritually impure
Most of it
The בית המקדש area (the Temple)
Wood from the מזבח's woodpile

phrases.english: MISHNA: If the whole [Paschal lamb] or most of it became impure
they burn it before the Temple
with wood from the altar's arrangement.
phrases.notes: Wood from the public supply meant for the מזבח

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the earlier discussion of טומאת התהום
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A פסח that is wholly or mostly טמא is burned publicly in front of the בירה with wood from the מערכה.

steps.title: A slightly impure or leftover פסח is burned at home
steps.stepSummary: If only a small part became טמא, or if meat was left over (נותר), the owners burn it in their own yards or on their roofs with their own wood. Only stingy people burn it at the בירה, to use the free wood.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a minority of it became טמא, and also for the leftover meat, they burn it in their courtyards or on their roofs, with their own wood. Stingy people burn it in front of the בירה so they can use the wood of the מערכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the second case. A small part טמא, or leftovers, are burned privately at home, with the owners' own wood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the owners are not required to burn it publicly, so they must supply their own wood. The משנה adds that some stingy people still bring it to the בירה, just to save money by using the public wood.

keyTerms.meaning: A minority (small part) of it
Meat left over past its time, which must be burned
Their courtyards
Their own wood
The stingy people

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the stingy people as doing something forbidden. The משנה is describing what they do. Burning at home is the normal practice here, and the stingy people choose the בירה to save on wood.

phrases.english: If a minority of it became impure, and the leftover
they burn it in their courtyards
or on their roofs, with their own wood.
The miserly burn it before the Temple
in order to benefit from the wood of the arrangement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the contrasting case to step 27: minority טמא or נותר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A partly טמא or leftover פסח is burned at home with private wood. The stingy may burn it at the בירה to use public wood.

steps.title: Why must a mostly impure פסח be burned in front of the בירה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the rule that a wholly or mostly טמא פסח must be burned publicly at the בירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks why the first case requires burning in front of the בירה. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the second case the owners may burn it at home. So why does the first case require a public place? The גמרא wants to know the logic behind this difference.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion of the משנה
What is the reason?

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: Why must the wholly or mostly impure פסח be burned in front of the בירה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the ruling in step 27
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason a wholly or mostly טמא פסח must be burned publicly at the בירה

steps.title: The public burning is meant to embarrass the owners
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר חנינא explains that the public burning is meant to embarrass the owners.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר חנינא said: In order to embarrass them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי בר חנינא answers the question. They burn it publicly so the owners will feel ashamed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If all or most of the קרבן became טמא, the owners were probably careless with it. Burning it in a public place lets everyone see, and the shame teaches them to be more careful. A small amount of טומאה is not treated as such serious carelessness, so no public burning is required.

keyTerms.meaning: To embarrass them

steps.whatToRemember: Wholly or mostly טמא means public burning at the בירה, to shame careless owners. Minority טמא or נותר means private burning with the owners' own wood.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina said:
In order to embarrass them.
phrases.notes: They were presumably careless, so the burning is done publicly

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא כְּדֵי לְבַיְּישָׁן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 29
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The public burning is meant to shame owners whose carelessness let the קרבן become mostly טמא.

steps.title: A contradiction from meat carried out of ירושלים begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rule that a minority-טמא פסח is burned at home. It cites another משנה about someone who left ירושלים with קודש meat. That משנה says that if he passed צופים he burns it where he is, and if not, the rule continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said, 'If a minority of it became טמא,' and so on. Raise a contradiction: Similarly, someone who left ירושלים and remembered that he has holy meat in his hand: if he passed צופים, he burns it where he is; and if not...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes our משנה's case of a minority טמא and starts to set another source against it. This line is a setup, and the end of the contradicting source, with the actual clash, comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה lets the owners burn a partly טמא or leftover פסח anywhere at home. The other source deals with קודש meat that became disqualified by leaving ירושלים. It says that only if he is already far away (past צופים) may he burn it where he is. The suggestion is that if he is still close, he must go back and burn it in ירושלים, in a special place. That would seem to clash with burning freely at home.

keyTerms.meaning: And raise a contradiction (set one source against another)
Meat of a קרבן
Mount Scopus, the point from which ירושלים can still be seen
In his current place

steps.confusionAlert: The quoted source is cut off at 'וְאִם לָאו'. The full contradiction only becomes clear on the next amud, so do not try to finish the argument yet.

phrases.notes: Quoting our משנה

and remembered that there is consecrated meat in his hand,

he burns it in his place,

steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that a partly טמא or leftover פסח may be burned at home with private wood
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another משנה implies that disqualified קודש meat must sometimes be brought back to ירושלים to be burned. That seems to contradict the freedom to burn at home.
